title: Use dashboards to check a system's health

blocks.content: A dashboard is a saved page of panels, one place to check whether a system is healthy. Someone builds it once, and from then on anyone can open it and read it without writing a query. In this guide you'll walk through a dashboard of a wind farm that tracks power produced, turbine speed, and wind, all on the same page, updating as you watch.
First, find a dashboard and open it.

Click **Dashboards** in the main menu.

This page lists every saved dashboard, grouped in folders.

Open **Demo Wind Farm**, one of the dashboards in the **Examples** folder.

It watches a small wind farm and shows power produced, turbine speed, and wind.
You opened a saved dashboard from the dashboard list. No setup, just a click.
Next, read the dashboard and try its controls.

blocks.reftarget: [data-testid='data-testid Panel header Wind Farm - Total Average Power (Watts)']
blocks.content:
Look at the chart tracking the farm's power output over time.

Each rectangle on the page is a panel, one view of the data. Others show single numbers, like **Current Power**.
blocks.tooltip: One view of the data. A dashboard is a saved page of these.

blocks.content:
Watch the **Current Power** panel as its menu opens.

Every panel has one. It hides in the panel's top-right corner until your mouse is over the panel, and it lets you view, share, or inspect just that panel.

steps.tooltip: This panel, like every panel, keeps a menu in its top-right corner.
The menu lives here. **View**, **Share**, and **Inspect** give you a closer look at this one panel.

blocks.content:
Open the **time range** picker at the top right and choose **Last 1 hour**.

The time range sets the window of time the whole page shows. When it changes, every panel on the page redraws to the new window at once.

steps.tooltip: The window of time the whole page is showing. Every panel follows it.

steps.reftarget: [data-testid='data-testid TimePicker time range option now-1h to now'] label
steps.tooltip: One change here redraws every panel on the page for the new window of time.

blocks.content: Change the time range once and every panel follows. That's enough to read almost any dashboard you meet in Grafana Cloud.
